purpose: First REAL card golden. Two scenarios: (A) reproduces SBI's own worked example from the e-kit PDF pg 33 (the issuer did the arithmetic for us), proving cap + exclusion + floor logic on real terms; (B) a steady-state annual case that binds the online cap, for the optimiser/evaluator path.

scenario_A_pdf_worked_example.purpose: Single statement-month, matches PDF pg 33 exactly.
_hand_computation: PDF states: total spend 45,000 = online 35,000 + offline 10,000; of online, 10,000 was an EMI purchase.
EMI purchases are excluded from cashback -> eligible online = 35,000 - 10,000 = 25,000.

scenario_B_steady_state_annual.purpose: Annual steady-state, uniform seasonality, binds the online monthly cap. This is the value the optimiser selects on.
scenario_B_steady_state_annual._spend_annual_note: Keys use the golden-battery's own 'category[/channel]' convention (tests/test_goldens.py::_parse_spend_annual) -- category choice (ecommerce, offline_retail) is arbitrary within online_5pct/offline_1pct's channel-only selectors (they don't constrain category), picked only because both have a Rs0-floor-loss ticket size at these rates (Rs1800*5%=Rs90.00, Rs1500*1%=Rs15.00 exactly, see docs/DECISIONS.md).
_hand_computation: Online monthly cashback = 50,000 x 5% = 2,500, BUT online cap = 2,000/cycle -> capped to 2,000. Overflow earns zero.
Offline monthly cashback = 20,000 x 1% = 200 (below offline cap 2,000).
Waiver-eligible annual spend = 8,40,000 >= 2,00,000 -> renewal fee WAIVED -> steady-state fee = 0.

_notes: Scenario A is the strongest possible correctness check: the issuer published the expected answer.
Scenario B deliberately drives online spend past the 2,000 cap so the golden tests cap-binding + overflow=zero, not just linear accrual.
Both use channels (online/offline), which exercises channel-based selectors on real data.
If either scenario is red, the bug is in the engine or the bundle, NOT the expected values (arithmetic shown above).
